toolDesc.ask_question: Ask the user to clarify requirements or confirm information. Preset options are provided, and the user can also add answers that are not in the options through the free-input box.
toolDesc.create_agent: Create an agent (prompt preset); its content is injected as a system prompt
toolDesc.create_kanban_task: Create a task card on the board (column, priority, assignee, due date, and linked project can be specified)
toolDesc.create_memory: Save a long-term memory (user preference, important fact, project convention); supported scopes: Global (shared) / Project
toolDesc.create_project: Create a managed project (local directory or SSH remote directory); it appears on the Projects page
toolDesc.create_scheduled_task: Create a scheduled task that runs automatically on its schedule. Supports running skills, custom AI tasks, rebuilding the knowledge graph, and rebuilding Embeddings. A task can be bound to the current session, and its results are appended to this session.
toolDesc.create_skill: Create a built-in skill (database skill); a skill is triggered by /name or use_skill
toolDesc.create_workflow: Create a workflow (nodes + edges); run it on the Workflows page or via run_workflow
toolDesc.delete_agent: Delete an agent (irreversible; built-in agents cannot be deleted)
toolDesc.delete_note: Delete a note (moved to the trash, recoverable)
toolDesc.delete_project: Delete a managed project (removes the entry only; files on disk are untouched)
toolDesc.delete_tag: Delete a tag (only untags notes, does not delete them)
toolDesc.get_usage_stats: View LLM usage stats: cumulative and today's message/Token counts, average duration, daily trend, and model distribution
toolDesc.list_agents: List available agents (database + local directory: name/category/type/whether it is a specialized agent)
toolDesc.list_inbox_items: View inbox notifications (system/scheduled task/workflow/board task); filtering by category and archive state is supported
toolDesc.list_kanban_tasks: View the task board (cards grouped by column: title/status/priority/assignee/due date/linked project)
toolDesc.list_knowledge_items: Browse what the knowledge base already holds (notes, files, URLs)
toolDesc.list_memories: Browse the long-term memory list (by scope/category: Global / Session / Project)
toolDesc.list_note_versions: View the version history of a note (version IDs and save times)
toolDesc.list_notebooks: View the notebook tree (with each notebook's ID and hierarchy)
toolDesc.list_notes: Browse notes by criteria (filter by notebook, tag, or favorites; or sort by keyword); returns titles and excerpts
toolDesc.list_projects: List all managed projects (name/group/category/tags/directory/linked Code project)
toolDesc.list_scheduled_tasks: View all scheduled tasks (name, type, schedule, enabled state, next run time, last result)
toolDesc.list_skills: List all locally configured skills (name, description, category) for running skill-specific tasks
toolDesc.list_tags: View all tags (including the number of notes under each)
toolDesc.list_wiki_docs: List Wiki docs (grouped by project: title/type/updated time/collection)
toolDesc.list_work_projects: List the projects that can be mounted in the Code view (name/root directory/session count/connected MCP and skills)
toolDesc.load_tools: Load the full parameter docs of tools on demand (a session keeps only basic tools resident by default; other tools must be loaded before they can be called)
toolDesc.move_kanban_task: Move a task card to a target column (blocked reason optional)
toolDesc.move_note: Move a note to a specified notebook (or out of its notebook)
toolDesc.plan: Submit an execution plan to the user for confirmation. Meant for multi-step tasks, tasks with side effects, or tasks with a wide blast radius: list the plan steps first, execute after the user approves, and revise the plan based on feedback if it is rejected.
toolDesc.read_knowledge_item: Read the full content of a knowledge base item (Markdown/plain text)
toolDesc.read_wiki_doc: Read the body of a Wiki doc (Markdown)
toolDesc.restore_note_version: Roll a note back to a specified historical version
toolDesc.run_command: Run a command (on Windows use cmd.exe syntax, such as echo, dir, type, findstr; on macOS use zsh/bash syntax, such as echo, ls, cat, grep; on Linux use bash syntax, such as echo, ls, cat, grep)
toolDesc.run_workflow: Run a workflow and return the result (including details of failed nodes)
toolDesc.search_graph: Search entities and relations in the knowledge graph
toolDesc.search_web: Search the web for the latest information
toolDesc.set_note_tags: Set the tags of a note (full replacement; pass the complete list of tag IDs; an empty list clears the tags)
toolDesc.todo: Plan and track your work steps. Rules: (1) when a complex task arrives, first use action=create to break it into multiple sub-steps; (2) before starting a step, call action=update to set its status to in-progress; (3) as soon as a step is done, call action=complete to mark it finished; (4) this flow is mandatory: call complete once for every finished sub-step, do not wait until the end to update; (5) for update/complete prefer the id returned by create, or match exactly by title.
toolDesc.update_agent: Update an agent (name/category/prompt/type/bound model, etc.); pass only the fields to change
toolDesc.update_inbox_items: Batch-process inbox notifications: mark read/unread, archive/unarchive, delete
toolDesc.update_kanban_task: Update a board task: title, description, priority, assignee, tags, due date, blocked reason
toolDesc.update_project: Update a managed project: name, description, category, tags, directory
toolDesc.update_skill: Update a built-in skill (name/description/category/config/enabled state); pass only the fields to change
toolDesc.update_tag: Change a tag's name or color
toolDesc.update_workflow: Update a workflow (name/description/nodes/edges/enabled state); pass only the fields to change
toolDesc.use_skill: Load the full instructions of an enabled skill by name, then complete the task following them
toolDesc.work_apply_patch: Make an exact text replacement inside a file: replace the search snippet with the replace snippet; search must match exactly once (or use replaceAll to replace every occurrence)
toolDesc.work_delete_file: Delete a single file in the project (path relative to the project root)
toolDesc.work_diagnostics: Run build/static-check commands in the project (such as dotnet build, tsc, npm run build) and return compile errors and warnings, for self-checking after code changes
toolDesc.work_git: Run read-only git queries (status/diff/log/show/blame/branch, etc.) and return the command output
toolDesc.work_glob: Find file paths in the project by glob pattern (such as **/*.cs, src/**/Work*.tsx); returns paths relative to the project root
toolDesc.work_grep: Search file contents in the project with a regular expression; returns file:line:content
toolDesc.work_list_dir: List the sub-directories and files of a directory in the project (relative to the project root)
toolDesc.work_move_file: Move or rename a file in the project (from → to, both relative to the project root)
toolDesc.work_read_file: Read file content in the project (path relative to the project root)
toolDesc.work_run_command: Run a shell command in the project (working directory and timeout optional); returns stdout/stderr and the exit code
toolDesc.work_semantic_search: Describe the logic you are looking for in natural language and retrieve project code snippets by meaning (requires the project to have a code index)
toolDesc.work_skill: Load the full instructions of an enabled skill by name, then complete the remaining steps following them (covers database skills, the local skills directory, and the project's .github/skills)
toolDesc.work_task: Dispatch a read-only sub-agent to investigate independently inside the project (it can read files and search code) and return a summary of its findings. Suited to cases that require going through many files while the main flow only needs the conclusion
toolDesc.work_write_file: Create or overwrite a file in the project (path relative to the project root); content is the complete file content
toolGuide.ask_question: Prefer clarifying when a request has ≥2 reasonable interpretations or key information is missing; always confirm with this tool before destructive operations (delete/overwrite/clear).
toolGuide.create_agent: Use when the user asks to create an agent/role; write the system prompt in content (role, responsibilities, output requirements) and keep the name short; use list_agents first to avoid duplicate names.
toolGuide.create_kanban_task: Cards land in Backlog by default; use Medium when the user gives no priority, and never assign an owner on your own.
toolGuide.create_memory: Call it proactively when you spot a user preference/fact worth remembering long-term (such as "I use PostgreSQL"); in a Code session, to save project-level facts (tech stack, architecture conventions, lessons learned) pass scope=Project and get projectId via list_projects; do not save information that is only temporary within a session (session memory is extracted automatically by the system).
toolGuide.create_note: Call it only when the user explicitly asks to save/note down/organize something as a note; use search_notes first to confirm there is no duplicate note.
toolGuide.create_notebook: Call when the user asks for a new category/notebook; if a notebook with the same name already exists, tell the user instead of creating a duplicate.
toolGuide.create_project: Call when the user explicitly asks to create a project; the directory path must be confirmed by the user — never invent a path.
toolGuide.create_scheduled_task: Call when the user asks for something to run on a schedule/periodically/every day/every hour. The task type and schedule must be clear. Once bound to the current session, every run result is appended to this conversation.
toolGuide.create_skill: Use when the user asks to turn a process into a skill; use list_skills first to confirm no skill has the same name, and name it in kebab-case (such as weekly-report). config is a JSON string and may contain fields such as promptTemplate and tools.
toolGuide.create_tag: Use list_tags first to check whether a tag with the same name already exists, to avoid duplicates.
toolGuide.create_workflow: Use when the user asks to solidify a multi-step process into a workflow. nodes is a JSON array string whose elements look like { "id": "n1", "type": "start|agent|tool|condition|loop|parallel|merge|human|subworkflow|end", "label": "node title", "agentId": "agent GUID (for agent nodes)", "config": "node config JSON (for tool nodes, the tool name etc.)", "x": 0, "y": 0 }; edges look like { "id": "e1", "source": "n1", "target": "n2", "sourceHandle": "true" }. Field names must match exactly as above (label, not name; source/target, not from/to). Verify with list_workflows after creating.
toolGuide.delete_agent: Use when the user explicitly asks to delete an agent; always report the name/ID back to the user for confirmation before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_kanban_task: Destructive operation: confirm the task title with the user via ask_question before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_memory: Call when the user explicitly asks to forget something/delete a memory; restate the memory content to the user for confirmation before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_note: Call when the user explicitly asks to delete a note; confirm the note title and ID with the user before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_project: Destructive operation: you must confirm the project name and ID with the user via ask_question before calling.
toolGuide.delete_scheduled_task: Call when the user explicitly asks to cancel/delete a scheduled task; identify the target with list_scheduled_tasks first and tell the user the task name before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_skill: Use when the user explicitly asks to delete a skill; always report the skill name/ID back to the user for confirmation before deleting.
toolGuide.delete_tag: Destructive operation: confirm the tag name via ask_question, then delete.
toolGuide.delete_workflow: Use when the user explicitly asks to delete a workflow; always report the name/ID back to the user for confirmation before deleting.
toolGuide.get_usage_stats: Call when the user asks how many tokens were used or how much was spent; do not tack stats onto every conversation.
toolGuide.list_agents: Call when the user asks which agents are available or who to ask for something; this tool is for display and recommendation only and cannot switch the current persona.
toolGuide.list_inbox_items: Call when the user asks what notifications there are or whether any scheduled task failed; use update_inbox_items to act on them.
toolGuide.list_kanban_tasks: Call it first whenever the user mentions tasks, to-dos, the board, or progress; card status values are Backlog/Todo/InProgress/InReview/Blocked/Done/Archived.
toolGuide.list_knowledge_items: Call when the user asks what is in the knowledge base or which materials are indexed; to retrieve actual content use search_notes or search_graph instead.
toolGuide.list_memories: Call when the user asks what you remember about them, their preferences, or this project's conventions; for semantic retrieval use search_memory instead.
toolGuide.list_note_versions: Call when the user wants to recover old content or see what was changed in a note; once you have a version ID you can roll back with restore_note_version.
toolGuide.list_notebooks: Call it before organizing notes or browsing by category to get notebook IDs; the tree structure is expressed through parentId.
toolGuide.list_notes: Call when the user asks what notes they have, what they wrote recently, or what is under a notebook; when the title keyword is known, prefer search_notes.
toolGuide.list_projects: Call it first when the user mentions my projects or a certain project, to get the project ID and directory before doing anything else.
toolGuide.list_scheduled_tasks: Call when the user asks which scheduled/automatic tasks exist, or why a task failed last time.
toolGuide.list_skills: Call it first when the user asks to use a skill / run skill X, to get the skill ID; the skill ID is also needed when creating a scheduled task that runs a skill.
toolGuide.list_tags: Call it before browsing by tag or tagging notes to get tag IDs.
toolGuide.list_wiki_docs: Call when the user asks what is in the Wiki or about a certain project's docs; once you have the doc ID, read the body with read_wiki_doc.
toolGuide.list_work_projects: Call when the user asks in chat which projects can be coded on; unlike the file tools, it needs no project context.
toolGuide.list_workflows: When the user asks to run some process, call this first to confirm the workflow ID and whether it is enabled, then run it with run_workflow.
toolGuide.load_tools: For tools listed under on-demand loading in the system prompt, load their parameter docs with this tool before calling them: pass tool names or group names in names (such as the task board group), or search by keyword with query (such as query="board"); resident tools need no loading.
toolGuide.move_kanban_task: A target of Done means completed; when the target is Blocked you must provide blockedReason.
toolGuide.move_note: Call when the user asks to organize notes or to file a note under a notebook; leaving notebookId empty moves the note out of its notebook.
toolGuide.plan: When a request involves ≥2 execution steps or has side effects such as writes, deletes, or installing dependencies, submit a plan and wait for the user's approval before acting; do not overuse it for simple, single-purpose requests.
toolGuide.read_knowledge_item: Get the item ID with list_knowledge_items or semantic retrieval first; cite as [[title]] when referencing it.
toolGuide.read_note: Call when search_notes returns candidate notes and you need the full content; do not read the same note repeatedly.
toolGuide.read_wiki_doc: Get the doc ID with list_wiki_docs first; when the body is long, quote only the key passages and cite as [[Wiki title]].
toolGuide.restore_note_version: Call after the user confirms they want the old version back; get the version ID with list_note_versions first, and tell the user the current content will be overwritten before rolling back.
toolGuide.run_command: For read-only diagnostics only (Windows: dir, type, findstr, echo %VAR%; macOS/Linux: ls, cat, grep, echo, etc.); any write operation or command containing rm/format/del must be confirmed via ask_question first; never run commands that could harm the system.
toolGuide.run_workflow: Use list_workflows first to confirm the workflow is enabled and is the one the user really wants to run; workflows may call tools and models internally, so they are heavy operations — run once, do not retry in a loop.
toolGuide.search_graph: Call when the user asks about relations between concepts, related notes, or the knowledge landscape; for single-fact lookups prefer search_notes.
toolGuide.search_memory: Call when you need to consult the user's long-term preferences, past conclusions, or important facts; it complements search_notes — memory covers personal preferences, notes cover knowledge content.
toolGuide.search_notes: When a question touches the user's own notes, call this tool first and answer from the results; never answer questions about the user's private notes from memory alone.
toolGuide.search_web: Call when a question involves real-time information (news, prices, version numbers, recent events) or facts you are unsure about; do not call it for purely subjective questions or questions about the user's private notes.
toolGuide.set_note_tags: Call when the user asks to tag or tidy up a note's tags; get tag IDs with list_tags first — never invent IDs from names.
toolGuide.todo: For tasks with ≥2 steps you must first list all atomic sub-steps with create; before starting each step update→in-progress; complete as soon as it is done. Batch-completing is forbidden, and so is leaving steps until the end to update them all at once.
toolGuide.update_agent: Use when the user asks to adjust an agent's prompt or attributes; get the id with list_agents first; fields you do not pass keep their current values.
toolGuide.update_inbox_items: Confirm with ask_question before deleting notifications; read-only operations (marking as read) can be executed directly.
toolGuide.update_kanban_task: Get the task ID and current fields with list_kanban_tasks first; pass only the fields that need to change and keep the rest as they are. Use move_kanban_task to change columns.
toolGuide.update_note: Read the current content with read_note first so you do not overwrite the user's recent edits; confirm with ask_question before major rewrites.
toolGuide.update_project: Get the project ID with list_projects first; pass only the fields that need to change.
toolGuide.update_skill: Use when the user asks to rename a skill, change its description, or disable/enable it; get the id with list_skills first; fields you do not pass keep their current values.
toolGuide.update_tag: Get the tag ID with list_tags first; renaming affects every note carrying that tag, so confirm the new name with the user.
toolGuide.update_workflow: Use when the user asks to adjust a workflow's nodes or to enable/disable it; get the id with list_workflows first; fields you do not pass keep their current values.
toolGuide.use_skill: The skill list in the system prompt gives only names and one-line descriptions; when a skill clearly matches the current task, call this tool to read the full instructions before acting.
toolGuide.work_apply_patch: Prefer this tool when editing existing files; use work_write_file only to create a file or rewrite it entirely.
toolGuide.work_delete_file: Use only when the user explicitly asks to delete a file.
toolGuide.work_diagnostics: After changing code, prefer calling this tool to verify rather than guessing. Leave the command empty to auto-detect by project type; the first detection result suggests a command you can pin in the project settings.
toolGuide.work_git: Use when looking at version history and changes; for write operations such as commit or push, use work_run_command.
toolGuide.work_glob: Prefer it when locating files, instead of walking directories level by level with work_list_dir.
toolGuide.work_grep: Use to locate code symbols or text; pattern uses .NET regex syntax.
toolGuide.work_run_command: Only for development operations such as build, test, lint, and git; destructive commands (delete, format, shutdown, etc.) are forbidden.
toolGuide.work_semantic_search: Use it when you know what logic you want to find but not the keywords; when you know the exact symbol name, prefer work_grep — it is faster and more accurate.
toolGuide.work_skill: Skills listed in the system prompt come with only a name and a one-line description; when a skill clearly matches the current task, call this tool to read the full instructions before acting.
toolGuide.work_task: One sub-agent does one thing; state the goal, the file scope to focus on, and the expected output format in prompt. Sub-agents cannot modify files — make the changes yourself if needed.
toolGuide.work_write_file: Only for creating a file or rewriting it entirely; to change part of an existing file use work_apply_patch.
